inputs.original_text: This is the familiar reflex to treat the state’s security concerns as suspect while demanding courtroom-level proof before authorities can act. A reported link to a Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri” may not prove guilt, but it is hardly a reason to dismiss national-security concerns out of hand. The state must act lawfully, but protecting the country and maintaining public order are not optional—and those who invoke liberty should not pretend suspicion carries no risks when national security is at stake.
inputs.modified_text: A reported link to the Karachi-based “Punjabi Kuri” is not proof of guilt, but it is enough to warrant serious scrutiny—not reflexive suspicion of the state. A country’s first duty is to protect its people and preserve public order, while acting lawfully. Liberty matters, but it cannot mean authorities must wait for courtroom-level proof before addressing a potential security risk. Those demanding restraint should also reckon with the consequences of ignoring warning signs.
